prize_parts.citation: For discoveries of the physiology of glucagon-like peptide-1 and of its biologically active form, which made possible incretin-based therapy for type 2 diabetes and obesity

statement.case_for: GLP-1 remains the strongest achievement on the shortlist on originality, mechanistic clarity, independent replication and impact. Holst established secretion and glucose-dependent insulinotropic action in humans, Drucker defined proglucagon-derived peptide biology and receptor actions, and Mojsov identified and synthesised the active truncated peptide that made the physiology tractable. The clinical consequence is confirmed in large independent randomised trials for glycaemia, weight, cardiovascular and renal outcomes, and nobody has raised a maturity objection. I have changed my configuration from round 1: I now credit Mojsov instead of Knudsen as the third name. My reason is the scope of the citation. If the prize honours discovery, which is where the committee has most often drawn its line, then identification of the bioactive peptide is a discovery contribution in its own right, whereas analogue engineering inside a company programme is a development achievement, however decisive for patients. This is a change of judgement on credit scope and not a response to the count of five colleagues who already hold this trio.
statement.case_against: The weak point is attribution, and I do not think it is resolved. Habener's group on proglucagon and GLP-1 is outside the credited names and Mojsov's priority against it cannot be settled from the supplied record, so my trio may rest on a contested chronology. Leaving out Knudsen means the drugs patients actually take, liraglutide and semaglutide, are credited to nobody, and the prize could be read as honouring the idea but not the medicine. The three-name cap makes every B004 configuration partial, and a citation worded around physiology and the active form carries that uncertainty openly rather than removing it.

responses.point: Perlmann argues that Knudsen's work optimises a molecule that follows from the discovery, and that a physiology-centred trio of Drucker, Holst and Mojsov keeps the prize on discovery while treating the Knudsen omission as the strongest objection.
responses.response: In round 1 I weighed analogue development more heavily and said I could accept Mojsov if the citation were confined to discovery. After your argument I accept that condition. The Nobel logic here is the biology of GLP-1 and its active peptide, and drug optimisation is a downstream step even though the clinical impact depends on it. I still think the Knudsen omission is a real cost and the citation should not suggest the prize covers the drugs themselves. I would, however, keep the wording close to your formulation, with the active form named explicitly, so that the choice of Mojsov is visible and justified by the citation.

responses.point: The chair distinguishes Mojsov's discovery contribution from industrial analogue design and does not regard imatinib (B007) as overdue in a way that outweighs GLP-1, given the Lasker 2009 recognition and the incomplete origin story.
responses.response: I agree on the first point and have moved accordingly. On B007 I have also moved: my round-1 preference for imatinib was driven by maturity and the clarity of the proof of concept, but the upstream credit gap (Philadelphia chromosome, BCR-ABL) lies outside the credited trio and cannot be repaired within the three-name limit. I would still keep it as my first alternative, since the demonstration that inhibiting a driver kinase controls a cancer has decades of survival data. I do not accept that the Lasker alone makes it ineligible, but I accept that it does not displace GLP-1. On your question about Habener, I think the citation wording should carry the uncertainty and the choice of laureates should not be changed by a priority claim we cannot document.

responses.point: Linnarsson moved from his opening trio to Drucker, Holst and Mojsov after reading colleagues' attribution arguments, and ranks the unfolded protein response (B032) as a clean, mature basic discovery.
responses.response: Your move is the same as mine, and I think the attribution arguments justify it. On B032 I agree that Walter and Mori form a clean two-person story with mature evidence, and I do not hold its limited therapeutic output against it. I still rank it below candidates with demonstrated patient benefit, because its disease relevance is inferred across many settings. Since a second prize part would cap the union at three people and shrink the B004 trio to two or even one, I do not think the quality of B032 changes the case for a single part this year.

responses.point: Wahren-Herlenius calls optogenetics (B043) mature and overdue as a method, and notes that its six credited names cannot be split fairly among three places.
responses.response: I agree on maturity and that the method has changed how causal questions are asked in neuroscience, which I see in my own field. I disagree that this makes it overdue in the sense a mature therapy is, and your own point about six claimants for three places is decisive for me. Nagel, Hegemann, Bamberg, Deisseroth, Boyden and Miesenboeck all have documented claims, and any trio would be disputable. I keep B043 as an alternative for that reason rather than as a preference, and I would prefer a configuration in which the committee does not need to adjudicate a tool's credit among six people.

responses.point: Sandberg asked what holds the B004 ranking back for El-Manira and describes B047 (SMN2 antisense) as a clear mechanism-to-drug link with a recent approval and competing SMA therapies.
responses.response: My opening ranking reflected the credit uncertainty and not doubt about the science, and I have since concluded that unresolved priority is a reason to word the citation carefully and not a reason to rank the achievement lower. On B047 I agree the mechanism-to-drug link is clear. I still place it behind the more established candidates because competing SMA therapies narrow the claim of Krainer and Bennett to a specific modality, and because it is a rare-disease story. I would not take it as the second part this year.

uncertainties: Whether Mojsov's priority for the active GLP-1 peptide holds against Habener's group; the supplied record does not settle it.
Whether the committee accepts a discovery-scoped citation that leaves the long-acting drugs, and so Knudsen, uncredited.
Whether a second prize part has any case strong enough to justify reducing the B004 trio, which I judge it does not this year.
Whether imatinib (B007) will be read as a development prize given the uncredited upstream discoveries and the 2009 Lasker award.
statement.conflict_note: Unchanged from round 1. My profile documents shared work with Thomas Perlmann (a 2009 paper on stem-cell-derived dopamine neurons), with Sten Grillner (the 2019 Physiol Rev synthesis) and with Patrik Ernfors. None of them is a credited name on any shortlisted ballot. My field of circuit neuroscience is nearest to B043 (optogenetics) and B047, but I have no documented tie to the credited names and no recusal-level conflict for my preferred B004 configuration.
